fields.description: Follow-up to roll-lqjj.53.1: incremental projection catch-up (read_tails, appended) still read appended segment and attempt bytes into Value trees and re-serialized each to hash it through Journal::add; the history cache was JSON arrays of Values; FileKey's 56-byte encoding was written twice; read_json_keyed did not presize its buffer. Read catch-up batches straight into a journal (projection::Appended), keep the cache in projection::codec, one FileKey::bytes.

data.text: Committed on branch perf/catch-up-lines-history-codec (198a35d + docs fixup): catch-up reads tails into projection::Appended via add_segment/add_attempt; <ws>/history in projection codec (magic 'bead history 2'); FileKey::bytes shared; read_json_keyed presized. ./check.sh green (1522 tests, doctests, 30 infra), clippy/doc/fuzz clippy clean, xtask tests rerun on HEAD. Not yet timed; not pushed. Review round 1 (3 findings) addressed in 9a6eadf: Appended::add_segment rejects an unterminated tail (test a_tail_ending_in_a_line_not_yet_whole_is_declined); read_keyed/read_json_keyed reserve with try_reserve_exact via read_up_to (OutOfMemory error, test a_read_with_no_room_for_its_length_is_an_error_not_an_abort); from_cached bounds capacity by bytes/25 and grows changed_fields. fields.title: Propagate accepted-attempt allocation errors and verify the history row bound

data.text: Fixed both follow-up review findings in 40fe52b on perf/catch-up-lines-history-codec. Journal replay returns a path-bearing IO error on accepted-attempt allocation failure. The history decoder checks that all rows fit before reserving, and its test covers both sides of the 25-byte boundary. Removing each guard in a scratch copy failed its regression test. The full baseline passed (1,526 nextest, 16 doctests, 30 infra), as did the workspace and fuzz lints and the docs build. Ready to land with roll-0668.

fields.title: Skip redundant transaction replay work and reject overflowing history counts

data.text: Addressed all three findings in 343ba7c on perf/catch-up-lines-history-codec. The waiting-cause transaction test converted one record batch before and zero after. The shared varint reader rejects an overflowing tenth byte, and malformed JSON alone now exercises the unreadable-line check. All three regression tests failed with their protections removed. The full baseline passed (1,528 nextest, 16 doctests, 30 infra), as did workspace and fuzz lints and the docs build. Ready to land with roll-0668.

fields.title: Bound nested cache allocations and verify that transactions skip batch preparation

data.text: Fixed AU06 and AU07 in 3d4a75a on perf/catch-up-lines-history-codec. The shared codec bounds all nested container reservations by the reader input and reserves fallibly. The waiting-cause regression calls Materialized::ensure and observes the emitted cause exactly once, after full replay starts. Both regressions failed under their respective mutations. Fast baseline passed (1,529 nextest, 16 doctests, 30 infra), as did workspace and fuzz lints and the docs build. Ready to land with roll-0668.

fields.title: Enforce projection and history contracts at public entry points and stress-test the branch

data.text: Fixed the public extension and history contracts and corrected the strict/lenient release note. The first independent whole-branch review found a store catch-up ordering issue, the history decoder documentation overpromised canonical validation, and its depth-boundary test only exercised the writer. All three are addressed, with segment and attempt read counts and independent encoded-input tests. Rechecking the full branch and stress suite.

Commit d136be0 on perf/catch-up-lines-history-codec passed ./check.sh --stress with 1,534 workspace tests, 16 doctests, 30 infra tests, and both six-machine stress models. The earlier overlapping baseline had one timeout in the private-repo prune test. That test passed in 54 seconds in the isolated full run. Workspace and fuzz formatting, Clippy, and rustdoc also passed. Started the next independent review against main.

The second whole-branch review reproduced full replay for unchanged files that share the cache timestamp on a projection waiting for a cause. AU14 now distinguishes verifying existing checksums from collecting added records. The regression test counted two segment reads before the change and one afterward. The attempt-file case and all 39 projection tests also passed.

The next review identified source compatibility, avoidable index decoding, and two test gaps (AU15–AU20). The old Rust entry points now coexist with the new binary and line-batch paths. A fresh downstream crate compiled the original inferred collections and round-tripped both conversion APIs. The saved projection records extension eligibility with checksummed source metadata, so missing/replaced attempts and checksum mismatches can fall back before the index is read. Differential tracks now prepare records once per batch. Focused tests and lints passed; running the full baseline, stress lanes, and another whole-branch review.

AU21 covered a new cloned-batch caller retaining operation payloads in the projected ancestry after updates were superseded. Copy-on-write now detaches the applied handle and leaves the caller’s original operation intact. A metadata-level regression test failed before the fix and passed afterward for both extension and replay. Rerunning the reviewer’s same allocator probe reduced live bytes from 1,078,310 to 23,861 for the cloned batch (moved batch 23,773).

Review of fcee796 found two further allocation regressions. Snapshot now shares its original event metadata with its replay. The new pointer-identity test failed on fcee796. The store drops verified source paths before allocating the index and hands only checked buffers to the core decoder. Repeated the original probes: the 10,000-event snapshot retains 6,422,397 bytes and the 5,000-attempt decode peaks at 8,548,145 bytes, both matching main. Stress, lints and another independent whole-branch review follow.

Complete on feature commit 8cee8b9aec833bb073aa5f079400532bb180775a. Independent full-branch review of its tree d26c746 against main a5fee69 found no actionable regression. All 1,540 workspace tests, 16 doctests, 30 infra tests, both six-machine stress scenarios (2,400 model operations and 3,000 concurrent commands), and 12,000 release differential seeds passed. Formatting, workspace and fuzz Clippy, and rustdoc passed. A 200,000-event standalone replay peaked at 105,574,808 heap bytes. The snapshot and cache allocation checks match main. No hosted PR exists for this branch. Releasing the claim pending integration.

AU24 reproduced against 8cee8b9 at the public API: the complete update requested and loaded the expected issue, while the same batch with a partial trailing line still requested it. The branch fix represents unchanged, replay and try-apply as distinct plans, with a checked readable batch required for text selection.

A fresh branch review found AU25. A torn segment still parsed its complete prefix after the newline check failed. The builder now drops its journal on a read error and skips later input. The parser-count regression failed before the fix and now passes, and the original 1,024-event heap probe went from 5,083,727 additional bytes to zero. Re-running the full suite and independent review.

AU26 found that an unreadable line in a complete catch-up segment still caused later lines to be parsed. The catch-up reader now shares journal decoding and event installation but stops on the first syntax error or missing event ID. A two-mode regression failed on the extra parse before the change and passes with full replay still collecting the error and later valid event. All 21 focused tests passed.

Final feature head 748aa23430ae3c10f184987f316df73d71c47f99. Independent review of its full tree against main found no actionable regressions and all 26 reviewer-selected tests passed. Verification passed: 1,543 workspace tests, 16 doctests, 30 infrastructure tests, both six-machine stress models, 12,000 differential seeds, workspace/fuzz formatting and Clippy, and rustdoc. The incomplete 4,430,769-byte segment retained zero additional heap bytes. Catch-up stops at the first unreadable record and full replay still recovers later valid events. Releasing this branch-only work pending integration.

Reopened for AU27. The builder had stopped parsing after rejection, but collecting its input still advanced a lazy producer. Adding a public producer-visit regression and a transaction replay check for the unconsumed suffix.

fields.description: create --parent, update ending a claim and close/delete ending a claim each open-code: drop what the write held, publish_soon, read the store again. Unlike cli::finish (roll-lqjj.50) none asks beadroll_sync::destination first, so offline or on a tracker with no remote each frees the transaction (~83 ms at 200k events) and rereads a state although nothing was exchanged. create --parent also inserts a string 'unpublished' that note_unpublished overwrites with the count. Fix: one consuming helper that chooses the destination first and hands what was held back when nothing is exchanged.
fields.title: Mid-command publishers hand-order Spent disposal: create --parent frees and rereads with nowhere to publish

data.text: Committed on fix/mid-command-publish: publish_first helper in commands/publish.rs used by create --parent, update, transition; held.rs read-count test, publish_on_write black-box tests, heap guard. ./check.sh green (1557). Next: codex review loop.

fields.description: Pre-existing on main (found by the codex review of roll-e3pu). When .beadroll.json names one remote where the store coordinates through another, cli::finish's publish_soon_at returns 'recorded locally, not yet published (CONFIG)' and pushes it to the human lines only; note_unpublished then finds unpublished_count Ok(None) (ws.endpoint errs) and adds nothing. So 'bead create x --json', 'comments add --json', 'dep add --json' etc. exit 0 with no unpublished field and empty stderr although nothing was published. create --parent, update and transitions carry the words in their result. Fix: finish says it in --json too (an unpublished string on object results, or a stderr warning) when no count stands.
fields.title: A write whose remote cannot be chosen says so to --json nowhere

fields.description: Pre-existing on main (found by the codex review of roll-e3pu, which pinned crates/beadroll/src/testing.rs tracker() and its own fixture with Machine::with_bead(built_bead())). Still unpinned: crates/beadroll/src/cli/ending.rs a_write_on_a_tracker_with_no_remote_keeps_what_it_held_when_the_process_ends_with_it (Machine::new), and crates/beadroll-sync/src/link/merge/tests.rs machines a and b. With BEAD_UNDER_TEST naming another binary, that binary initialises the store this build then reads in process, which can fail in setup rather than in what the test checks. Pin each with .with_bead(built_bead()), as main.rs's rust_only does for black-box tests.

data.text: Branch fix/mid-command-publish (4 commits, a27c3b4) clean after 4 codex rounds (gpt-6.2-astra xhigh). Claim 1 confirmed and fixed (publish_first). Claim 2 refuted in part: the string 'unpublished' is the only --json signal where no count can be made (CONFIG remote), so it stays; plain create's silence there is roll-gy2j. Pre-existing unpinned in-crate fixtures: roll-gzcr. Not yet on main: not pushed, no PR.

fields.description: Pre-existing on main (seen in the codex review of roll-e3pu). transition::superseded words every stale end it finds as 'another owner took over before this close reached the remote; it is ignored'. A close can also be stale with one owner and no remote: an event waiting in a cycle of causes keeps the claim off the frontier the close builds on, and with the clock behind the claim replay orders the close first (hardening::superseded_owner_close_says_so::a_close_replay_ignores_is_superseded_with_nothing_published). The answer is right to say superseded; its words should say why from what the stale entry and the claim's history show, not assume a takeover.
fields.title: A close replay ignores for its order says another owner took over when none did

fields.description: Pre-existing on main (seen in the codex review of roll-e3pu). transition looks up superseded only when its publish gave no warning: a close or delete naming the claim it ends whose publish failed (REMOTE_UNREACHABLE, CONFIG) answers 'unpublished' and never asks the store whether replay took the end, though replay can put it before its claim with nothing exchanged (an event waiting in a cycle of causes keeping the claim off the frontier, the clock behind the claim; hardening::superseded_owner_close_says_so::a_close_replay_ignores_is_superseded_with_nothing_published) and a failed exchange may have fetched a takeover before it failed. The absence of superseded then says nothing. Consider looking it up whenever a claim was named, warning or not.
fields.title: A close whose publish fails never says replay ignored it

fields.description: Pre-existing on main (seen in a review of roll-e3pu). journal::active_segment names the next segment {n:06}.jsonl and segment_files lists them in name order, so after 999999.jsonl comes 1000000.jsonl, which sorts before it: replay reads the new segment first, the chain breaks, and the store can read as NOT_INITIALIZED or lose issues. Reproduced with the branch binary on unchanged code: rename a fresh tracker's 000001.jsonl to 999999.jsonl, then BEAD_ROTATE_BYTES=1 bead create plain --json succeeds and bead list --json answers NOT_INITIALIZED. active_segment also takes segments.last() by name, which stays 999999 after the rotation. Reachable at the default 256 KiB only after about 244 GiB of one machine's journal, or with a tiny BEAD_ROTATE_BYTES. Fix: refuse (IO) a rotation whose next name sorts before the last, or order segments by number (format 1 is frozen: additions only, so check what readers older builds tolerate). The commands that answer from their write (create, update, comments, and since roll-e3pu create --parent and an offline update/reopen ending a claim) report success then; main's update ending a claim answered ISSUE_NOT_FOUND only after the write had committed.
fields.title: Past segment 999999 a journal's next segment sorts before it, and the tracker no longer reads

fields.description: Left by the whole-project audit (roll-23jk, 2026-11-09) for the maintainer, never filed until now. AGENTS.md says errors carry codes a user can act on and that `bead prime` lists them, and docs/REVIEWING.md:142 says `bead prime` lists the codes, but prime's RULES block (crates/beadroll/src/cli/texts.rs) names 14 of the 27 in crates/beadroll-core/src/code.rs. Missing on main at f7e0d30: ATTEMPT_FORK, CONFIG, FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED, GIT_ERROR, IDENTITY, JOURNAL_FORK, KEY_SPACE, MANIFEST_MISSING, NO_REMOTE, NO_WORKSPACE, NOT_INITIALIZED, USAGE, WORKSPACE_MISMATCH. An agent that meets one of them has nothing in its session's workflow to say what to do.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Either prime names every code in code.rs with what to do about it, or REVIEWING §2 records which codes prime leaves out and why, and the docs that say prime lists them say what it lists. A test keeps prime's list and code.rs in step, so a new code cannot be added without deciding.
fields.title: bead prime lists 14 of the 27 error codes a command can answer

fields.description: Seen 2026-11-27 on the maintainer's Mac (macOS 27.2) running ./check.sh on fix/mid-command-publish, which touched none of these tests' code paths. Four full runs: two red, each with different failures; every failing test passed alone (8 and 5 consecutive runs) and in the other full runs, and CI on PR #322 was green. (1) storage::projection::deferred::writes_in_a_row_leave_the_projection_until_the_records_after_it_are_many: 'write 11: the records before it are few', the stored projection rewritten where the test expected it left (deferred.rs:120). (2) protocol::ownership_races::six_simultaneous_claims_have_one_winner: 'cannot start target/debug/bead: No such file or directory' (machine.rs:258) though the binary's mtime showed no rebuild during the run. (3) protocol::unanswered_releases::timed_out_release_fenced_by_its_own_next_round_is_built_again: UNRESOLVED 'git push gave no answer within 1s' (unanswered_releases.rs:148), under load. Not obviously the same cause as roll-x9x5 (lock-order in parallel tx unit tests) or roll-ui9r (infra's shebang-less stand-ins).
fields.acceptance_criteria: Each of the three is explained, from a reproduction under load (for example nextest with a high --test-threads, or a stress loop) or from reading its timing assumptions, and fixed or given a deadline that load cannot reach; or each is shown to come from something outside the suite, which is then recorded. ./check.sh is green in ten consecutive full runs on that machine.
